source.notes: Compiled from hospital/clinic patient handouts (Stanford 2012, Kaiser Permanente SF 2023, MNGI Digestive Health 2026, GastroClinic (Stanford derivative), Cleveland Clinic, Johns Hopkins (via Wayback), Mayo Clinic Press (search snippet only; site blocks fetch), Michigan Medicine intro PDF (contains no food list; full lists are handed out by RD only)), NHS sheets (Cambridge CUH, Gloucestershire, Southampton gentle low FODMAP, KCL/Guy's & St Thomas' booklet sample pages), Canadian Digestive Health Foundation, ACG, and Monash-trained dietitian lists (Kate Scarlata 2020 checklists + grocery list, IBS Diets food list + chart, FODMAP Everyday 2017 list, A Little Bit Yummy portion posts). Ratings: high = avoid at a normal serving; moderate = low only at the restricted serving in lowServing; low = low at a typical serving. null = not a source of that group or not stated. Group attributions come from CDHF/Mayo/Stanford/FE where stated, otherwise inferred from Monash-published composition and flagged in notes. Serving sizes are per meal/sitting; sources differ substantially (see disagreements). Older handouts (Stanford 2012, KCL 2014) predate Monash re-testing and are more conservative on vegetables. Fun Without FODMAPs publishes recipes only; no public food list with servings was found.

foods.name: onion
foods.notes: Universal 'avoid entirely' item in every handout, including onion powder, onion salt, dried onion, onion extract and 'flavouring' on labels. Hidden in stocks, gravies, soups, sauces, marinades, ready meals, flavored chips. Fructans are not oil-soluble, so onion-infused oil is low. CUH allows 2 large pickled onions (45 g). UHS reintroduction challenge starts at 1 tbsp.
disagreements: Stanford lists 'onion powder' in the Foods to Eat column while listing onions in Foods to Limit; every other source treats onion powder as a concentrated high-fructan ingredient

foods.name: garlic
foods.notes: Universal avoid, including powder/salt/puree/extract. Garlic-infused oil (strained) is low in all sources because fructans are water-soluble, not oil-soluble. CUH allows 1 clove pickled garlic (20 g). UHS reintroduction starts at 1/4 clove. Common in restaurant sauces, pesto, hummus, tzatziki, marinades, chorizo.
disagreements: Stanford lists 'garlic powder' and 'garlic flavored oil' as Foods to Eat while listing garlic in Foods to Limit; all other sources treat garlic powder as high

foods.name: garlic-infused oil
foods.notes: Recommended onion/garlic substitute in IBS Diets, Kate Scarlata, CUH, Glos, Kaiser, MNGI, UHS, Stanford. Must be strained oil, not 'garlic extract'. FODMAP-free because fructans are not oil-soluble.

foods.name: shallot
foods.notes: Listed as high with onion in IBS Diets, Kate Scarlata, Kaiser, Glos, FODMAP Everyday, ACG.

foods.name: leek
foods.notes: Bulb/white part is high fructan (IBS Diets, Kate, Kaiser, CUH, UHS, ACG, CDHF). Green leaves are low (IBS Diets, Kate, CDHF 1 cup, MNGI 'leaves only'). UHS reintroduction starts at half a leek.

foods.name: scallion
foods.notes: Green part is the standard low-FODMAP onion substitute in every handout; white bulb is high fructan.

foods.name: artichoke
foods.lowServing: canned artichoke hearts (CUH: low; Glos: <3 tbsp)
foods.notes: Fresh globe and Jerusalem artichoke high in all handouts. Canned/marinated hearts are lower because fructans leach into brine (CUH, FE list canned hearts low). Group inferred: fructans (Jerusalem: inulin), globe also fructose per Monash.

foods.name: asparagus
foods.notes: High in all handouts. CDHF and Mayo Connect attribute it to excess fructose; Kaiser/Kate/CUH list it without group. Glos prints it in both columns with an asterisk (very small quantities <3 tbsp).
disagreements: Glos NHS: tolerated in very small quantities (<3 tbsp/day); all others: avoid

foods.name: cauliflower
foods.notes: Polyol (mannitol) source per CDHF, Mayo, Kate, FE. UHS reintroduction starts at 2 tbsp.

foods.name: mushroom
foods.lowServing: oyster mushrooms unrestricted; canned button mushrooms (FE, CUH); dried porcini 2 tbsp/15 g (CUH)
foods.notes: Mannitol source (CDHF, Mayo Connect, FE). Oyster mushrooms are low in Kate, IBS Diets, CDHF, ACG, CUH, FE. Canning leaches mannitol so canned button mushrooms are low (FE, CUH). UHS reintroduction starts at 2 tbsp.
disagreements: FODMAP Everyday 2017 list includes fresh 'Mushroom, button' as low; IBS Diets, Kate Scarlata, Kaiser, MNGI, CUH, Glos, UHS, ACG list fresh button mushrooms high

foods.name: oyster mushroom
foods.notes: Only common fresh mushroom that is low in all sources that list it (Kate, IBS Diets, CDHF, ACG, CUH, FE, ALBY).

foods.name: broccoli
foods.lowServing: heads 3/4 cup (IBS Diets, CDHF, CDHF fibre); Kaiser 1/2 cup; MNGI 1/2 cup; FE3 75 g
foods.highServing: FE3: 270 g florets; stalks lower serve (IBS Diets 1/3 cup)
foods.notes: Fructan content is dose dependent. Heads are lower than stalks per IBS Diets (Monash). CUH 'broccoli tenderstems' 3 tbsp/45 g.
disagreements: Stanford (2012): broccoli in Foods to Limit
Kate Scarlata, ACG, FE, CUH: low with no stated limit
Glos NHS: very small quantities (<3 tbsp)

foods.name: broccolini
foods.notes: Heads are higher than stalks (opposite of broccoli).

foods.name: brussels sprout
foods.notes: Fructan source per Mayo Connect and CDHF. Listed as avoid by Stanford, Kate, Kaiser, Mayo Press, CDHF; small serves allowed by IBS Diets, CUH, Glos (asterisk), FE (low).

foods.name: cabbage
foods.notes: Common green/red/white cabbage is low in most Monash-based lists.
disagreements: Stanford 2012 and Kaiser 2023: cabbage in avoid list (no variety stated)

foods.name: savoy cabbage
foods.lowServing: IBS Diets: <1/2 cup; CUH <3 tbsp (55 g)
foods.notes: Higher fructan than common cabbage. Kate lists as high. FE 2017 lists 'Cabbage, Savoy' low.

foods.name: celery
foods.lowServing: < 5 cm stalk (IBS Diets); CUH 1/3 stick (15 g); MNGI 1/4 stalk; Kaiser 1 stalk
foods.notes: Mannitol source per CDHF and Mayo. Stanford lists celery as low with no limit.
disagreements: CDHF: polyol high (no low serve given)

foods.name: beet
foods.lowServing: canned or pickled: 1/2 cup (IBS Diets), 1/3 cup (CDHF); fresh 2 slices (Kaiser, CUH 25 g)
foods.notes: Fresh beet is high fructan (CDHF, Kate, Kaiser, IBS Diets, MNGI). Canned/pickled beet is low in IBS Diets, Kate, CDHF, CUH, FE2, Kate grocery. FE 2017 lists 'Beets' low without qualification.

foods.name: sweet potato
foods.lowServing: 1/2 cup / 75 g (IBS Diets, Kaiser, MNGI, CUH 3 tbsp, ALBY 75 g); CDHF 1/3 cup; Kate 1/2 small
foods.notes: Mannitol dose-dependent. Purple/white-fleshed sweet potato low up to 75 g per IBS Diets. Stanford lists 'yams' low and does not mention sweet potato.

foods.name: potato
foods.notes: FODMAP-free in all handouts (FE2 no-FODMAP list). CDHF prints '1/4 cup' which appears to be a transcription error. Plain baked potato/fries are a restaurant-safe starch (Kaiser, Glos).

foods.name: corn
foods.lowServing: 1/2 cob (IBS Diets, Kate, Kaiser, MNGI, CUH 40 g); canned 1/2 cup (CDHF), 1/3 cup (IBS Diets)
foods.highServing: CDHF: corn listed as polyol high; CUH loose sweetcorn 1 tbsp limit
foods.notes: Sorbitol + fructans dose-dependent. Stanford lists corn low unrestricted. Corn flour/polenta/tortillas are low (starch, not the kernel sugars).
disagreements: CUH: loose sweetcorn only 1 tbsp (15 g), cob 1/2

foods.name: green bean
foods.lowServing: 15 beans / 75 g (IBS Diets, CDHF, ALBY); Kaiser 1/2 cup
foods.notes: Low in every source except Stanford 2012, which lists green beans in Foods to Limit.
disagreements: All Monash-based sources: low at 15 beans

foods.name: green pea
foods.lowServing: CUH 1 tbsp (20 g); Kaiser 1/2 cup; CDHF fibre 1/4 cup; canned 2 tbsp (CUH)
foods.notes: GOS/fructan source (CDHF). Kate, MNGI, IBS Diets chart, FE list as high; Kaiser allows 1/2 cup.

foods.name: snow pea
foods.notes: Kate, Kaiser, MNGI, Stanford, CDHF: avoid. IBS Diets and CUH allow 5 pods.

foods.name: sugar snap pea
foods.notes: Excess fructose per CDHF and Mayo. Glos prints in suitable column; most others avoid.

foods.name: butternut squash
foods.lowServing: 1/4 cup (IBS Diets); 1/3 cup (MNGI); 1/2 cup (Kaiser); CUH <3 tbsp (60 g)
foods.notes: Stanford lists butternut low unrestricted. Glos: very small quantities.

foods.name: pumpkin
foods.lowServing: canned 1/4 cup (IBS Diets, Kate); fresh 63 g (IBS Diets)
foods.highServing: CDHF: pumpkin listed high (fructans and polyols)
foods.notes: Kabocha/Japanese pumpkin is FODMAP-free (FE2, ALBY2, Kaiser). Generic 'pumpkin' varies by type.
disagreements: IBS Diets: canned 1/4 cup, fresh 63 g

foods.name: kabocha squash
foods.notes: No detectable FODMAPs (FE2, ALBY2); Kaiser and Kate list low.

foods.name: spaghetti squash
foods.notes: Kate, CDHF2, FE, Kate grocery list low.

foods.name: zucchini
foods.lowServing: 65 g / 1/3 cup (IBS Diets, ALBY, MNGI); Kate 5-6 slices
foods.notes: Fructans dose-dependent per Monash-based sources. Stanford, Kaiser, CUH, Glos, FE, UHS list zucchini as low with no limit.

foods.name: yellow squash
foods.notes: Stanford 2012 lists 'summer squash' in Foods to Limit; all others low.

foods.name: eggplant
foods.notes: Low in every source.

foods.name: bell pepper
foods.lowServing: green 75 g / 1/4 medium; red 1/2 cup 43 g (IBS Diets); ALBY red 1/3 cup; Kaiser all colors unrestricted
foods.highServing: ALBY: 1 whole red pepper; CDHF: red/yellow/orange high (excess fructose)
foods.notes: Green pepper is the safer color. Red/yellow/orange contain excess fructose at larger serves (Monash 2022 retest reflected in CDHF/ALBY).
disagreements: IBS Diets/ALBY: red capped at 1/3-1/2 cup

foods.name: tomato
foods.notes: Fresh tomato low in every source. FE2 lists beefsteak as no-FODMAP (variable across batches). Monash 2022 retest found excess fructose at large serves, which is why IBS Diets gives 65 g.

foods.name: canned tomato
foods.lowServing: 1/2 cup (MNGI, CDHF); 3/5 cup (IBS Diets); 100 g per person (ALBY)
foods.highServing: ALBY: moderate-high at larger serves (excess fructose)
foods.notes: Base for homemade pasta sauce; commercial versions usually add onion/garlic.

foods.name: tomato paste
foods.highServing: Kaiser, MNGI: avoid (label ingredient to avoid)
foods.notes: Concentrated fructose. IBS Diets allows 2 tbsp; Kaiser and MNGI put tomato paste in the avoid column.

foods.name: tomato juice
foods.lowServing: 1/2 glass (IBS Diets, MNGI 1/2 cup); CUH 200 ml
foods.notes: FE lists tomato-based vegetable juice blends low.

foods.name: cucumber
foods.notes: Low in every source; FE2 no-FODMAP (variable).

foods.name: carrot
foods.notes: FODMAP-free in every source.

foods.name: lettuce
foods.notes: All varieties low; butter/red leaf/frisee FODMAP-free (FE2).

foods.name: parsnip
foods.notes: FODMAP-free (FE2, ALBY2).

foods.name: rutabaga
foods.lowServing: 1/4 cup (CDHF); unrestricted elsewhere (Kate, IBS Diets, CUH, FE)

foods.name: fennel
foods.lowServing: bulb 75 g / 1/2 cup (IBS Diets, Kaiser, MNGI); CUH 3 tbsp (60 g); Kate 'few slices'; leaves 15 g
disagreements: Stanford: fennel in Foods to Limit

foods.name: okra
foods.lowServing: 7 pods / 75 g (CDHF, CUH); MNGI 6 pods; Kaiser 1/2 cup
disagreements: Stanford: okra in Foods to Limit

foods.name: olive
foods.notes: Low in every source; check marinated olives for garlic.

foods.name: chili pepper
foods.notes: Low FODMAP but capsaicin is a gut irritant for some (IBS Diets 'if tolerable').

foods.name: ginger
foods.notes: FODMAP-free (FE2).

foods.name: chive
foods.notes: Standard onion substitute in every handout; FODMAP-free (FE2).

foods.name: seaweed
foods.notes: Nori is low in every source. CUH lists generic 'seaweed' in avoid but nori in suitable; IBS Diets lists kelp/kombu high.
disagreements: CUH: generic seaweed avoid, nori OK

foods.name: sauerkraut
foods.lowServing: 1/2 cup (IBS Diets); red cabbage sauerkraut 1/3 cup (CDHF)

foods.name: pickle
foods.lowServing: unrestricted (MNGI dill or sour pickle; IBS Diets pickled gherkins; FE gherkins in vinegar)
foods.notes: Sweet pickles/relish with onion or HFCS are high (IBS Diets 'relish/vegetable pickle'). Stanford lists 'pickle' in Foods to Limit without qualification.
disagreements: MNGI/IBS Diets/FE: plain dill pickles low

foods.name: cassava
foods.notes: Cassava flour is low per IBS Diets. Conflicting for the root.

foods.name: plantain
foods.notes: Kaiser, Kate, IBS Diets, CUH, FE list low.

foods.name: chicory root
foods.notes: Concentrated fructan/inulin. Flagged by Stanford, Kate, Kaiser, MNGI, CUH, Glos, IBS Diets, CDHF as a hidden ingredient in 'high fiber' cereals, bars, yogurts, plant milks, protein bars, chai/chamomile teas, coffee substitutes (Camp). Labels: inulin, FOS, oligofructose, 'prebiotic', chicory root fiber.

foods.name: endive
foods.notes: FODMAP-free (FE2). Not to be confused with chicory root.

foods.name: edamame
foods.lowServing: Kate: 2 handfuls; CUH 90 g; CDHF fibre 1/2 cup; ACG low
foods.notes: Immature soybean; lower GOS than mature soybeans.

foods.name: apple
foods.notes: Universal avoid in every handout: excess fructose plus sorbitol. Also apple juice, cider, applesauce, fruit teas containing apple, plant milks sweetened with apple juice. UHS reintroduction starts at 40 g.

foods.name: pear
foods.notes: Universal avoid; canned fruit in pear juice also high.

foods.name: watermelon
foods.notes: Universal avoid; CDHF lists it under fructans, excess fructose and polyols. UHS reintroduction starts at 40 g.

foods.name: mango
foods.notes: Excess fructose (CDHF, FE). Universal avoid.

foods.name: cherry
foods.notes: Excess fructose + sorbitol (CDHF, FE). Universal avoid.

foods.name: peach
foods.notes: Yellow peach = sorbitol, white peach = fructans (FE). Universal avoid; UHS reintroduction starts at 1/4 medium.

foods.name: nectarine
foods.notes: Universal avoid at normal serving.

foods.name: apricot
foods.notes: Fresh: sorbitol; dried: also fructans (CDHF). Universal avoid.

foods.name: plum
foods.notes: Prunes also high fructan (CDHF). Universal avoid.

foods.name: blackberry
foods.notes: Sorbitol (CDHF). Avoid in IBS Diets, Kate, Kaiser, MNGI, CUH, Glos, ACG, Mayo Press.

foods.name: fig
foods.notes: Fresh: excess fructose; dried: fructans (CDHF).

foods.name: date
foods.lowServing: IBS Diets: 1 date (dried pitted 5 dates per one IBS Diets line - inconsistent)
foods.notes: Avoid in Kate, Kaiser, MNGI, CUH, ACG, Glos. FE lists 'dates fresh' low. Common in energy bars and 'no added sugar' snacks.

foods.name: raisin
foods.lowServing: 1 tbsp (Kate); 1 tsp / 4 g (IBS Diets); CUH 12 g (<1 tbsp); Glos 1 tbsp
foods.notes: Dried fruit concentrates fructans; a 'dried fruit' avoid appears in Stanford, Kaiser, Kate, UHS, MNGI. Trail mix and granola typically exceed the low serve.

foods.name: dried cranberry
foods.notes: Usually sweetened; check for HFCS/apple juice concentrate.

foods.name: grapefruit
foods.lowServing: < 80 g (IBS Diets); CUH 1/2 medium (100 g); Glos <1/2 small
disagreements: Stanford: grapefruit in Foods to Eat
IBS Diets/CUH/Glos: half a fruit low

foods.name: pomegranate
foods.lowServing: Kate: handful; CUH 1/2 small (55 g); Glos 1/2 small

foods.name: lychee
disagreements: CDHF 'What can I eat': lychee listed low

foods.name: banana
foods.lowServing: 1 medium firm/unripe (IBS Diets, CDHF); Kaiser 1/2 banana; FE2 'up to 500 g'
foods.notes: Firm/just-ripe banana low in every source. Ripeness changes the rating (fructans accumulate as it ripens).

foods.name: ripe banana
foods.lowServing: CUH: 1/2 very ripe (<45 g); FE3: <35 g
foods.notes: Group: fructans per Monash-based sources (CDHF lists ripe banana under fructans). Cleveland Clinic says 'ripe bananas (fructose)' and FE3 says polyols; group inferred as fructans (Monash).
disagreements: Cleveland Clinic: fructose, up to 1/3 in cereal

foods.name: avocado
foods.lowServing: 1/8 avocado (Kaiser, MNGI); 3 tbsp / 60 g (IBS Diets); 3 slices (Kate); <1/4 (CUH, Glos)
foods.notes: Sorbitol dose-dependent. Restaurant guacamole portions typically exceed 1/8 avocado. Avocado oil is FODMAP-free.
disagreements: Stanford/GastroClinic: avocado listed as a stone fruit to avoid
Kaiser: 1/8 allowed but 'avocado' also appears in the vegetables-to-avoid list
FODMAP Everyday 2017 & Kate grocery list: listed low without limit

foods.name: blueberry
foods.lowServing: 1 cup (IBS Diets, CDHF, CDHF fibre, ALBY2, FE3 125 g); Kaiser 1/2 cup; MNGI 1/4 cup

foods.name: strawberry
foods.lowServing: 5 medium / 65 g (IBS Diets, ALBY); Kaiser 1/2 cup; others unrestricted
foods.notes: Listed low in every handout; the 5-berry cap comes from a Monash retest and only appears in newer dietitian sources.

foods.name: raspberry
foods.lowServing: 1/3 cup / 30 berries (IBS Diets, CDHF fibre); Kaiser 1/2 cup

foods.name: grape
foods.lowServing: unrestricted (Kate, Stanford, JH, ACG, CUH); IBS Diets chart 10-15 grapes; Kaiser 1/2 cup
foods.highServing: CDHF: grapes listed under excess fructose (high)
foods.notes: FE2 lists grapes as no-FODMAP but re-tested with variable results. Monash 2023 retest found excess fructose at larger serves.
disagreements: CDHF 'Understanding': grapes excess fructose high; CDHF 'What can I eat': grapes low

foods.name: orange
foods.notes: Whole orange low everywhere; juice is limited (see orange juice).

foods.name: pineapple
foods.lowServing: 1 cup fresh (IBS Diets, CDHF); Kaiser 1/2 cup
foods.highServing: dried pineapple (IBS Diets high; CUH 1 piece 25 g)

foods.name: papaya
foods.highServing: dried papaya (IBS Diets high; CUH 5 g)
disagreements: Stanford/GastroClinic: papaya in Foods to Limit

foods.name: guava
foods.highServing: unripe guava (IBS Diets); Stanford: guava limit
disagreements: IBS Diets: ripe low / unripe high

foods.name: cranberry
foods.lowServing: 1 tbsp (IBS Diets); Kaiser 1/2 cup fresh; MNGI raw allowed

foods.name: cranberry juice
foods.lowServing: 3/4 cup / 3/4 glass (IBS Diets, CDHF); MNGI 4 oz; CUH 250 ml
foods.notes: Must be 100% or without HFCS (Kate, Kate grocery, FE).

foods.name: coconut
foods.lowServing: fresh flesh 2/3 cup (IBS Diets); dried 1/4 cup (IBS Diets), 4 tbsp (CDHF), <3 tbsp (Glos), 45 g (CUH); Kaiser 1/2 cup dried
foods.highServing: Glos: dried coconut in large quantities; Stanford: coconut limit
disagreements: Stanford/GastroClinic: coconut, coconut milk, coconut cream in Foods to Limit
Kate/IBS Diets/CDHF/CUH/Kaiser/FE: low at stated serves

foods.name: coconut milk
foods.lowServing: canned 125 ml / 4 oz (IBS Diets, CUH, MNGI); CUH canned 60 ml as condiment; coconut cream 1/4 cup (IBS Diets), 1/2 cup (MNGI); Kaiser unrestricted
foods.highServing: ACG: carton coconut milk high; Stanford: limit
foods.notes: Canned (cooking) coconut milk is the low option; carton coconut milk beverages often add inulin. Kate: canned only.

foods.name: coconut flour
foods.notes: CUH and Glos list coconut flour in avoid; often used in 'grain-free' packaged snacks.

foods.name: coconut yogurt
foods.lowServing: unrestricted (IBS Diets, Kate, ACG, CUH, Glos, UHS, FE)
foods.notes: Check for inulin/chicory and fruit purees.

foods.name: rhubarb
foods.notes: FODMAP-free (FE2).

foods.name: tamarind
foods.lowServing: Kaiser low; CUH <5 (10 g), paste <3 tbsp

foods.name: canned fruit
foods.lowServing: canned mandarins / suitable fruit in suitable juice or syrup (CUH)
foods.highServing: canned fruit in apple or pear juice (IBS Diets, CUH, Glos); Stanford/Kaiser/MNGI: canned fruit avoid

foods.name: fruit juice
foods.lowServing: 125 ml / 1/2 cup of a low-FODMAP fruit only (IBS Diets, Stanford, GastroClinic, Glos 100 ml, UHS 150 ml/day)
foods.highServing: apple, pear, mango, guava, peach, tropical juices any amount; > 125 ml of any juice
foods.notes: Juice concentrates fructose. Fruit juice concentrate on labels is an avoid ingredient (Kaiser, MNGI, CUH).

foods.name: lemonade
foods.notes: Check sweetener; HFCS versions high.

foods.name: wheat bread
foods.notes: Fructans. Standard sandwich bread, bagels, pita, naan, ciabatta, focaccia, croissants, muffins, brioche all listed high. UHS reintroduction starts at 1 slice. Wheat as a minor ingredient (thickener, soy sauce) does not need avoiding (Glos, Stanford).
disagreements: FODMAP Everyday 2017: 'white bread' listed low (Monash small serve)

foods.name: sourdough bread
foods.lowServing: 2 slices (CDHF); 1 slice (MNGI); Kate 'slow leavened sourdough wheat or spelt'; ACG/JH not stated; FE whole-wheat sourdough low
foods.highServing: CUH/Glos: wheat sourdough is in the avoid list (only 100% spelt sourdough allowed); Glos 'small amounts may be ok'
foods.notes: Long fermentation degrades fructans. Supermarket 'sourdough' made with yeast and short proofing is not equivalent. Most restaurant bread is not true sourdough.
disagreements: CUH/Glos NHS: wheat sourdough avoid; spelt sourdough only

foods.name: spelt sourdough bread
foods.lowServing: 2 slices (CDHF fibre); unrestricted in CUH, Glos, UHS, IBS Diets, Kate, FE
foods.notes: The one wheat-family bread every NHS sheet allows. Must be true sourdough-leavened and 100% spelt.

foods.name: spelt bread
foods.lowServing: FE: 'spelt bread 100%' and 'spelt flour, organic sieved' low; Kaiser: spelt flour allowed ingredient
foods.highServing: CUH/Glos: spelt bread and spelt flour avoid (unless sourdough); Stanford: spelt is wheat, limit

foods.name: wheat pasta
foods.lowServing: 1/2 cup cooked (IBS Diets); FE 'wheat pasta, cooked' low (small serve)
foods.notes: Restaurant pasta portions (2+ cups) are far above the small low serve. Egg noodles, udon, ramen, gnocchi, couscous also high. UHS reintroduction starts at 5 tbsp cooked.

foods.name: gluten-free pasta
foods.notes: Avoid lentil/chickpea pastas (CUH, Glos: high GOS). Check for inulin or soy flour.

foods.name: chickpea pasta
foods.notes: CUH and Glos list red lentil and chickpea pasta as high even though gluten-free.

foods.name: gluten-free bread
foods.notes: Low only if free of high-FODMAP ingredients: check for inulin/chicory root, honey, apple/pear juice, soy flour, amaranth, dried fruit (Kate, Stanford, IBS Diets, Glos).

foods.name: rye
foods.notes: High in every source that lists it.

foods.name: wheat bran
foods.notes: Bran cereals are high in IBS Diets, CUH, Glos, MNGI.

foods.name: einkorn
foods.notes: Ancient wheats are wheat (Stanford lists einkorn/emmer/kamut/spelt as wheat terms; Kaiser: kamut avoid; IBS Diets: freekeh, einkorn flour high).

foods.name: amaranth
foods.lowServing: MNGI: 1/2 cup; FE: puffed amaranth low

foods.name: oat
foods.lowServing: 1/2 cup dry (Kaiser, MNGI, CDHF fibre, IBS Diets 1/2 cup oatmeal); unrestricted in Stanford, CUH, Glos, UHS, ACG, JH
foods.highServing: larger serves per Monash (not stated in handouts)
foods.notes: Low in every source. Instant flavored oatmeal packets may contain inulin or dried fruit. Oat-based biscuits/flapjacks allowed by Glos/CUH.

foods.name: oat milk
foods.lowServing: 30 ml for cereal (IBS Diets); 40 ml (CUH); 50 ml (Glos)
foods.notes: Oat milk in a latte typically exceeds the low serve. FE 2017 lists oat milk low without limit.

foods.name: quinoa
foods.lowServing: 1 cup cooked (CDHF); 3/4 cup (CDHF fibre); Stanford: 1/2 cup per meal if symptomatic
foods.notes: Low in every source. Stanford caps high-fiber low-FODMAP foods like quinoa at 1/2 cup/meal if symptoms occur, attributing symptoms to fiber load rather than FODMAPs.

foods.name: rice
foods.lowServing: 1 cup (IBS Diets, CDHF); unrestricted (ALBY2, Stanford, Kaiser)
foods.notes: FODMAP-free; safest restaurant starch (Kaiser eating-out tips).

foods.name: rice noodle
foods.notes: Asian rice-noodle dishes are recommended restaurant choices (Glos), but sauces usually contain garlic/onion.

foods.name: corn tortilla
foods.notes: Standard low-FODMAP wrap in Stanford, Kate, Kaiser, MNGI, CDHF. Flour tortillas are high (Stanford, Kaiser).

foods.name: corn chip
foods.notes: Plain corn/tortilla chips low in IBS Diets, Kate, Kaiser, MNGI, ACG, FE. Flavored versions often contain onion/garlic powder.

foods.name: corn flakes
foods.notes: Plain corn flakes low (IBS Diets, CUH, Glos, UHS, FE, Kaiser). Frosted/honey versions check sweetener.

foods.name: cheerios
disagreements: Stanford, Kate Scarlata grocery list, MNGI: low
Gloucestershire NHS: avoid (UK Cheerios are multigrain with wheat)

foods.name: granola
foods.notes: High in IBS Diets, Kaiser, CUH, Glos, MNGI because of wheat, dried fruit, honey, inulin, and sometimes cashews/pistachios. Gluten-free granola may still contain honey/dates.

foods.name: buckwheat
foods.lowServing: groats 1/2 cup, 100% buckwheat soba 1/3 cup (CDHF); unrestricted elsewhere
foods.notes: FE lists soba made with wheat and buckwheat low at a small serve; most restaurant soba is 20-40% wheat.

foods.name: tapioca
foods.notes: Pure starches are FODMAP-free (Stanford, Kate, CUH, Glos, MNGI).

foods.name: almond flour
foods.highServing: IBS Diets: almond meal high / high in large amounts
foods.notes: Common in grain-free and keto baked goods; a slice of almond-flour cake contains far more than 10 almonds.

foods.name: pizza
foods.lowServing: gluten-free base with tomato, cheese, ham, pineapple, suitable vegetables (CUH, Glos)
foods.highServing: regular wheat crust; any pizza with onion/garlic sauce
foods.notes: CUH and Glos list pizza/pizza bases high (wheat crust + garlic bread); GF pizza with chosen toppings is a recommended eating-out option (Glos). Sauce almost always contains garlic/onion.

foods.name: naan
foods.notes: All wheat breads (CUH, Glos, Kaiser, IBS Diets).

foods.name: pastry
foods.lowServing: filo 1 sheet, puff 1/4 sheet, shortbread 1 biscuit (IBS Diets); gluten-free versions with suitable sweeteners
foods.highServing: any wheat-flour baked good (CUH, Glos, Kaiser, MNGI)

foods.name: gnocchi
foods.notes: Wheat flour based (IBS Diets, CUH, Glos).

foods.name: breadcrumbs
foods.lowServing: gluten-free breadcrumbs, polenta, cornflake crumbs (CUH, Glos)
foods.highServing: wheat breadcrumbs/batter: fish fingers, tempura, schnitzel, nuggets, scotch eggs
foods.notes: Kate grocery lists Aleia's GF panko low.

foods.name: cracker
foods.lowServing: rice crackers, corn cakes, oatcakes (4), GF crackers; IBS Diets cream cracker 4; FE saltines low
disagreements: IBS Diets: 4 cream crackers low; FE: saltines low
CUH/Glos: cream crackers, water biscuits avoid

foods.name: pretzel
foods.lowServing: gluten-free pretzels (Kate grocery, MNGI, Kaiser); IBS Diets/Stanford: pretzels low

foods.name: potato chip
foods.notes: Flavored chips (sour cream & onion, BBQ) contain onion/garlic powder and are high (CUH, Glos).

foods.name: instant noodle
foods.notes: Wheat noodles plus onion/garlic seasoning (CUH, Glos).

foods.name: chickpea
foods.lowServing: canned, rinsed: 1/4 cup (IBS Diets, Kate, CDHF, MNGI, CDHF fibre); CUH 2 tbsp (44 g)
foods.notes: Canning leaches GOS into the liquid; rinse. Kaiser lists all beans avoid.

foods.name: lentil
foods.lowServing: canned, rinsed: 1/2 cup (Kate, MNGI), 1/3 cup (CDHF), 1/4 cup (CDHF fibre), 2 tbsp/44 g (CUH); boiled red/green 1 tbsp/23 g (CUH)
foods.highServing: typical serving of cooked-from-dry lentils; Stanford/Kaiser/JH/Glos/UHS: avoid

foods.name: black bean
foods.lowServing: canned, rinsed 1/4 cup / 45 g (IBS Diets, CDHF fibre)
foods.highServing: > 45 g; Kate, MNGI, FE, Mayo Press: avoid

foods.name: kidney bean
foods.lowServing: CUH: canned 8 tbsp (100 g) 'limited'; IBS Diets <85 g

foods.name: baked beans
foods.notes: Beans plus onion/garlic/HFCS sauce. Avoid in IBS Diets, CDHF, Kate, MNGI, ACG, Glos.

foods.name: lima bean
foods.lowServing: FE: lima beans boiled, butter beans canned rinsed low (small serve)
disagreements: FODMAP Everyday: low at small serve

foods.name: soybean
foods.notes: Mature soybeans and soy flour high (Kate, Stanford, IBS Diets, CDHF, CUH, Glos). Soy protein isolate, tofu and tempeh are different (see entries).

foods.name: tofu
foods.notes: Firm tofu low in every source except CDHF2 which lists 'tofu' among high-FODMAP proteins (probably meaning silken/soy generally). GOS drains off with the whey.
disagreements: CDHF 'What can I eat': tofu listed high
All others: firm tofu low; silken tofu high

foods.name: silken tofu
foods.notes: Retains whey and GOS (Kate, Kaiser, CDHF, IBS Diets).

foods.name: tempeh
foods.notes: Fermentation reduces GOS. Low in every source.

foods.name: hummus
foods.notes: Chickpeas + garlic. Avoid in IBS Diets, Stanford, Kaiser, CDHF, GastroClinic.

foods.name: soy milk
foods.lowServing: soy milk made from soy protein (not whole beans): low (IBS Diets, Kate, FE, GastroClinic); CUH 50 ml, Glos <60 ml of soya milk
foods.highServing: US-style soy milk made from whole soybeans (most brands)
foods.notes: US soy milk is usually made from whole beans (high). Australian brands made from soy protein isolate are low. Kaiser, MNGI, ACG, CDHF list soy milk high without distinction.
disagreements: IBS Diets/Kate/FE/GastroClinic: low if made from soy protein

foods.name: soy yogurt
foods.lowServing: 38 g (IBS Diets); 125 ml/125 g (CUH, Glos); UHS: low

foods.name: miso
foods.lowServing: IBS Diets, Kate grocery, FE, CUH: low (paste)
foods.highServing: Kaiser label list and GastroClinic: avoid

foods.name: quorn
foods.notes: Check ingredients: some Quorn products contain onion/garlic (Glos).

foods.name: pea protein
foods.notes: Note that whole green peas are high; the isolate is low.

foods.name: almond
foods.lowServing: 10 almonds / 12 g (IBS Diets, CUH, Glos, FE3); Kaiser 2 tbsp nuts; Kate 'one handful'
foods.highServing: 20 almonds / 24 g (FE3); IBS Diets almond meal high
foods.notes: Stanford lists nuts and almond milk low without limit. Almond butter 1 tbsp (Kate, Kaiser).

foods.name: almond milk
foods.notes: Low in every source (very dilute almond content). Check for added inulin or apple juice.

foods.name: cashew
foods.notes: One of the two universally avoided nuts (Kaiser, Kate, IBS Diets, CUH, Glos, Mayo, CDHF, ACG). Common in vegan cheeses, Thai/Indian dishes, trail mixes. FE 2017 lists 'cashews, activated' low.

foods.name: pistachio
foods.notes: Universal avoid.

foods.name: hazelnut
foods.lowServing: 10 nuts (IBS Diets chart, CUH, Glos); IBS Diets page says 24
foods.notes: Hazelnut milk low (CUH, Glos, UHS).

foods.name: peanut
foods.notes: Legume botanically but low FODMAP in every source.

foods.name: peanut butter
foods.notes: Check for added honey/HFCS (some US brands). Skippy, Smucker's, Teddie listed by Kate grocery.

foods.name: macadamia
foods.notes: Macadamia milk low (IBS Diets, Kaiser, CUH).

foods.name: pecan
foods.lowServing: 15 halves (IBS Diets, CDHF); IBS Diets chart 10 halves

foods.name: walnut
foods.lowServing: 15 halves (IBS Diets, CDHF); IBS Diets chart 10 halves

foods.name: pine nut
foods.lowServing: 1 tbsp (IBS Diets chart); 2 tsp (CDHF); unrestricted (Kate, Glos)

foods.name: chestnut
foods.notes: Chestnut flour is high (IBS Diets).

foods.name: chia seed
foods.lowServing: 2 tbsp (CDHF, ALBY); 1 tbsp (IBS Diets, CDHF fibre)

foods.name: hemp seed
foods.notes: Hemp milk low at 125 ml / 1/2 cup (IBS Diets, CUH, Kaiser).

foods.name: mixed nuts
foods.lowServing: mixes of low-FODMAP nuts only, one handful (Kate, Glos, FE)
foods.highServing: mixes containing cashews, pistachios, raisins, dates (IBS Diets)

foods.name: milk
foods.lowServing: Glos: 1/4 cup (50 ml) in a drink or meal; lactose-free milk unlimited
foods.highServing: a glass; UHS reintroduction starts at 125 ml
foods.notes: Universal avoid: lactose. Includes goat and sheep milk (Kaiser, Stanford, IBS Diets, CUH). Latte/cappuccino/milk tea are the usual restaurant exposure.

foods.name: lactose-free milk
foods.notes: Low in every source; the standard swap.

foods.name: evaporated milk
foods.notes: Dry milk solids and milk powder are label ingredients to avoid (Kaiser, MNGI). FE lists a Malaysian sweetened condensed milk low (outlier).

foods.name: cream
foods.highServing: IBS Diets: cream listed high in larger amounts

foods.name: whipped cream
foods.notes: Stanford lists whipped cream in Foods to Limit.

foods.name: sour cream
foods.lowServing: 2 tbsp (IBS Diets, Kaiser); lactose-free sour cream unrestricted (Kate)

foods.name: creme fraiche
foods.lowServing: CUH, Glos: low in small amounts

foods.name: yogurt
foods.lowServing: Greek yogurt 23 g (IBS Diets), 4 oz (MNGI); lactose-free or coconut yogurt unrestricted
foods.notes: Universal avoid for regular yogurt (lactose; fruit yogurts add fructose/inulin). GastroClinic lists Greek yogurt in the low-moderate column.

foods.name: lactose-free yogurt
foods.notes: Check for high-FODMAP fruit, inulin, HFCS.

foods.name: kefir
foods.lowServing: CUH: 1 tbsp; MNGI: allowed; Kate grocery: Lifeway plain kefir
disagreements: Kate grocery: plain Lifeway kefir low

foods.name: ice cream
foods.lowServing: 1 scoop (CUH, Glos); lactose-free ice cream 1/2-3/4 cup (Kaiser, CDHF); sorbet 1/2 cup (Kaiser, MNGI)

foods.name: custard
foods.lowServing: 2 tbsp (CUH, Glos); made with lactose-free milk unlimited

foods.name: hard cheese
foods.notes: Aged cheeses are virtually lactose-free; low in every source including Mayo, JH, UHS.

foods.name: brie
foods.notes: Stanford lists brie among soft cheeses to limit; all other sources low.

foods.name: cottage cheese
foods.lowServing: 2 tbsp / 40 g (IBS Diets, CUH, Glos); lactose-free cottage cheese unrestricted (Kate, Kaiser, MNGI); ACG/FE: low

foods.name: ricotta
foods.lowServing: 2 tbsp (IBS Diets, CUH, Glos); Kaiser 1/3 cup
disagreements: Kaiser: 1/3 cup allowed AND ricotta in avoid list

foods.name: cream cheese
foods.lowServing: 2 tbsp (IBS Diets, Kaiser, CUH, Glos); lactose-free cream cheese unrestricted (Kate)

foods.name: butter
foods.notes: Virtually zero lactose; low in every source. Ghee also low.

foods.name: dark chocolate
foods.notes: Low in every source; check for inulin, HFCS or polyols in 'sugar-free' bars.

foods.name: milk chocolate
foods.lowServing: 4 squares milk / 3 squares white (IBS Diets); 30 g (CUH, Glos)

foods.name: whey protein
foods.lowServing: whey protein isolate; egg, rice, pea, sacha inchi protein (IBS Diets, Kaiser, CUH)
foods.highServing: whey protein concentrate or hydrolysed (unless lactose-free); shakes with polyols, inulin or milk powder (IBS Diets, Kaiser, CUH, Glos)

foods.name: protein bar
foods.lowServing: brands with certified low-FODMAP logo (Kate grocery: 88 Acres, OWYN)
foods.highServing: most: chicory root/inulin, dates, honey, agave, maltitol/erythritol, whey concentrate, cashews
foods.notes: Kaiser: 'nutrition/granola/protein bars with high FODMAP ingredients' avoid; MNGI: high-fiber bars made with chicory root/inulin avoid; IBS Diets: fruit bars, muesli bars high. Group inferred from common ingredients.

foods.name: beef
foods.notes: FODMAP-free (FE2, ALBY2, all handouts). Restaurant risk is marinades, gravies, burger buns and seasoning blends with onion/garlic.

foods.name: chicken
foods.notes: FODMAP-free. Breaded/marinated/rotisserie versions often contain wheat, garlic, onion.

foods.name: pork
foods.notes: FODMAP-free. Check cured meats for honey glaze or garlic.

foods.name: fish
foods.notes: FODMAP-free; canned in brine or oil fine. Battered/crumbed fish is high (wheat).

foods.name: shellfish
foods.notes: FODMAP-free. Restaurant preparations often add garlic butter.

foods.name: egg
foods.notes: FODMAP-free in every source.

foods.name: deli meat
foods.lowServing: plain deli ham/turkey (Stanford, IBS Diets, Glos)
foods.highServing: varieties with garlic, onion, honey glaze, dextrose-fructose or wheat fillers (Cleveland Clinic 'processed meats')

foods.name: sausage
foods.lowServing: FE: German bratwurst low; sausages without garlic/onion/wheat filler (IBS Diets 'check ingredients')
foods.highServing: most sausages, hot dogs, chorizo, salami (garlic, onion, wheat rusk) per IBS Diets, ACG, Cleveland Clinic

foods.name: marinated meat
foods.lowServing: marinated in soy sauce, ginger, garlic-infused oil, herbs (Kaiser)
foods.highServing: marinades with garlic/onion, honey, agave, HFCS, molasses (Kate, Kaiser, MNGI, IBS Diets)

foods.name: breaded meat
foods.lowServing: coated in GF breadcrumbs, polenta or cornflakes (CUH, Glos)

foods.name: sugar
foods.notes: Sucrose is low FODMAP in every source (glucose:fructose 1:1).

foods.name: glucose
foods.notes: Allowed label ingredients in Kaiser, MNGI, CUH.

foods.name: corn syrup
foods.lowServing: Kaiser and MNGI: corn syrup (not high-fructose) allowed
foods.highServing: CDHF: 'corn syrup' listed under fructans high
foods.notes: Regular corn syrup is glucose-based; only HFCS is a fructose problem. CDHF's listing likely conflates it with HFCS.

foods.name: high-fructose corn syrup
foods.notes: Universal avoid (Stanford, Kate, Kaiser, MNGI, IBS Diets, CUH, Glos, CDHF, ACG). Found in US sodas, ketchup, jams, BBQ sauce, salad dressings, sweetened yogurt, cereal bars. Stanford notes a food can still be low overall if HFCS is the last ingredient.

foods.name: fructose
foods.notes: Label ingredient to avoid (Kaiser, MNGI, CUH, Glos).

foods.name: honey
foods.lowServing: Kate: small amounts in a product should be low enough (asterisk); IBS Diets: 1 tsp not stated, listed high
foods.notes: Excess fructose. Avoid in every handout: Stanford, Kate, Kaiser, MNGI, IBS Diets, CUH, Glos, CDHF, FE, Mayo. Common in honey-roasted nuts, granola, glazes, Asian sauces, 'natural' sweetened products.

foods.name: agave
foods.notes: Higher fructose than honey. Universal avoid.

foods.name: molasses
foods.lowServing: Kate: small amounts in a product OK; Glos lists treacle suitable
foods.highServing: Kaiser, MNGI, IBS Diets, CUH, GastroClinic: avoid
disagreements: Kate: small amounts in a product OK

foods.name: maple syrup
foods.notes: Low in every source (must be pure, not 'pancake syrup' with HFCS). FE2 lists as no-FODMAP (variable).

foods.name: rice malt syrup
foods.notes: Glucose/maltose based; low in IBS Diets, Kate, MNGI, FE2, Kaiser.

foods.name: stevia
foods.notes: Low in every source. Check blends for erythritol or inulin filler.

foods.name: aspartame
foods.notes: Non-polyol artificial sweeteners are low FODMAP (IBS Diets, CUH, Glos, Kaiser). CUH oddly also lists saccharin and cyclamate under polyol labels.

foods.name: sorbitol
foods.notes: Sugar-free gum, mints, candy, cough drops, 'diet' products (Stanford, Kate, Kaiser, CUH, Glos, MNGI).

foods.name: maltitol
foods.notes: Common in sugar-free chocolate and protein bars (MNGI lists hydrogenated starch hydrolysates and polydextrose).

foods.name: erythritol
foods.lowServing: IBS Diets: low; Glos: not listed
foods.highServing: Kaiser, MNGI, CUH: avoid (drinks with erythritol)
foods.notes: Absorbed in the small intestine so Monash rates it lower than other polyols, but several hospital handouts still avoid it.

foods.name: sugar-free gum
foods.lowServing: Kate grocery: Simply Gum (cane sugar based)
foods.notes: Called out by Stanford, Kate, Kaiser, KCL, CUH, Glos, MNGI. Polyol type varies: sorbitol, xylitol, mannitol, maltitol, isomalt.

foods.name: jam
foods.lowServing: strawberry/raspberry jam 2 tbsp (IBS Diets); 1.5 tbsp (Kaiser, MNGI)
foods.highServing: mixed berry, apple, apricot, fig jam; any with HFCS (Kate); Stanford: jams/jellies limit; low-sugar jams may contain polyols (Glos, CUH)
disagreements: IBS Diets/Kaiser/MNGI/Glos/CUH: low if suitable fruit and sweetener

foods.name: marmalade
foods.lowServing: unrestricted (IBS Diets, CUH, Glos, FE, Kate grocery)

foods.name: cocoa powder
foods.lowServing: 1 tbsp (IBS Diets, MNGI); cacao 1 tbsp/16 g

foods.name: hot chocolate
foods.lowServing: drinking chocolate powder 2 tsp (CUH) with lactose-free milk; IBS Diets: powder low
foods.highServing: Kaiser: hot chocolate and mix avoid; IBS Diets: malted chocolate drink high; made with cow's milk
disagreements: IBS Diets: malted chocolate drink high; FE: low

foods.name: coffee
foods.lowServing: 1 cup drip / 1 espresso shot (Kaiser, CDHF); with up to 250 ml lactose-free milk (IBS Diets)
foods.highServing: specialty espresso drinks with cow's milk or soy milk (CDHF); Kaiser: instant coffee avoid
foods.notes: Coffee itself is low FODMAP in every source but is a gut stimulant that can trigger IBS symptoms independently (Glos, IBS Diets). Latte with regular milk = lactose.

foods.name: black tea
foods.lowServing: weak black tea 1 cup (IBS Diets, CDHF, Kaiser, MNGI)
foods.highServing: strong black tea (IBS Diets: moderate/high fructans); black tea with soy milk
foods.notes: Milk tea with cow's milk = lactose.

foods.name: green tea
foods.notes: Low in every source; matcha 1 tsp (IBS Diets).

foods.name: peppermint tea
foods.notes: Low in every source; often recommended for IBS.

foods.name: chai tea
foods.lowServing: weak chai (IBS Diets, MNGI); Kate grocery: Tazo Chai Classic
foods.highServing: strong chai, chai latte (IBS Diets, Kate, Kaiser, MNGI, CUH, CDHF, ACG); chai with chicory root

foods.name: chamomile tea
foods.notes: High in IBS Diets, Kate, Kaiser, MNGI, CUH, CDHF, ACG. MNGI qualifies 'with chicory root'.

foods.name: dandelion tea
foods.highServing: strong (IBS Diets, CUH); chicory-based coffee substitutes (CUH, Glos)

foods.name: herbal tea
foods.lowServing: weak, without apple or chicory (IBS Diets, MNGI)
foods.highServing: strong herbal tea; fruit teas containing apple, pear, or chicory root (IBS Diets, CUH, Glos)

foods.name: kombucha
foods.notes: Fermented tea; FODMAP content varies with brand, sugar and fermentation. Group inferred (fructans/sorbitol per Monash).

foods.name: soda
foods.lowServing: sucrose-sweetened soft drinks (ACG); IBS Diets 'fizzy drinks without HFCS' in low quantities
foods.highServing: any soda sweetened with HFCS (IBS Diets, Kaiser, MNGI, ACG); CDHF: cola regular and diet high
foods.notes: US sodas are HFCS-sweetened; Mexican Coke / cane-sugar sodas are low FODMAP but carbonation can aggravate bloating.

foods.name: diet soda
foods.lowServing: ACG: diet soft drinks low; IBS Diets: sugar-free fizzy drinks low quantities
foods.highServing: CDHF: diet cola high; any diet drink sweetened with polyols or containing erythritol (Kaiser)

foods.name: sports drink
foods.notes: IBS Diets: sports drinks high; Kaiser: Emergen-C, Vitamin Water avoid (HFCS/fructose/polyols).

foods.name: meal replacement drink
foods.notes: IBS Diets and Glos: contain milk protein/lactose, inulin, FOS, polyols.

foods.name: rice milk
foods.lowServing: 200 ml (IBS Diets, CUH, Glos); unrestricted (Stanford, Kate, Kaiser)

foods.name: vegetable juice
foods.highServing: blends with beet, celery, apple; Stanford: high-FODMAP vegetable juices

foods.name: beer
foods.lowServing: 1 bottle/can: 12 oz (Kaiser, MNGI), 375 ml (CDHF), 'one' (IBS Diets); ACG/CUH/Glos/Kate/FE: low
foods.notes: Despite being wheat/barley-based, fermentation leaves beer low FODMAP at one serving. Alcohol itself is a gut irritant (Glos, IBS Diets).

foods.name: wine
foods.lowServing: 1 glass: 150 ml (CDHF), 4-6 oz (MNGI), 4 fl oz (Kaiser); dry red/white/sparkling (Kate, IBS Diets, CUH, FE)
foods.highServing: more than one glass (IBS Diets); sweet/dessert wine
foods.notes: CDHF lists only white and sparkling; CUH lists red, white and sparkling. FE lists sweet wine low, conflicting with Kaiser/CUH/Glos.

foods.name: dessert wine
foods.notes: Residual fructose. Avoid in Stanford, GastroClinic, Kaiser, CDHF, CUH, Glos.

foods.name: rum
foods.notes: Only spirit consistently listed high (Kate, Kaiser, IBS Diets, MNGI, CDHF, CUH, Glos, ACG, FE). Group inferred (fructose from sugarcane processing per Monash).

foods.name: vodka
foods.notes: Low in every source. Watch mixers (fruit juice, regular soda with HFCS, tonic is fine).

foods.name: cocktail
foods.lowServing: spirit + soda water, lime, or sucrose-sweetened tonic
foods.highServing: cocktails with fruit juice, agave (margarita), honey, rum, or HFCS syrups (CUH)
foods.notes: Group inferred from typical ingredients.

foods.name: hard cider
foods.notes: Apple-based; not explicitly listed in these handouts but apple juice is universally high. Group inferred.

foods.name: soy sauce
foods.notes: Low in every source despite containing wheat: fermentation removes fructans (Stanford, Kaiser, Kate, IBS Diets, CUH, MNGI, FE). Tamari is wheat-free.

foods.name: oyster sauce
foods.lowServing: < 2 tbsp (CUH); unrestricted (IBS Diets, Kate grocery, FE)

foods.name: worcestershire sauce
foods.notes: Low despite containing some onion/garlic and molasses (tested low by Monash).

foods.name: mustard
foods.notes: Low in every source; check honey mustard.

foods.name: mayonnaise
foods.lowServing: unrestricted (no garlic/onion); Kate grocery lists brands
foods.notes: Low in Stanford, Kaiser, Kate, IBS Diets, MNGI ('real' mayo), FE. MNGI: Miracle Whip avoid (HFCS). Aioli = garlic = high.

foods.name: ketchup
foods.lowServing: 1 sachet (IBS Diets US); 1 tbsp (Kate); 2 sachets/13 g outside US (IBS Diets); FE 'preferably no HFCS'
foods.highServing: Kaiser, GastroClinic: ketchup avoid; Kate: ketchup with HFCS avoid
foods.notes: US ketchup typically contains HFCS and onion powder.

foods.name: barbecue sauce
foods.lowServing: IBS Diets/FE: low if label free of HFCS, onion, garlic (rare in US)
foods.highServing: most commercial BBQ sauces (IBS Diets chart: 'BBQ sauces & marinades with HFCS/garlic')

foods.name: pesto
foods.lowServing: < 1 tbsp (IBS Diets); FE lists pesto low (Monash small serve); Stanford meal idea uses pesto
foods.highServing: standard recipes contain garlic (IBS Diets chart, UHS)
disagreements: IBS Diets chart/UHS: standard pesto high (garlic)

foods.name: tzatziki
foods.notes: Yogurt plus garlic (IBS Diets).

foods.name: pasta sauce
foods.lowServing: homemade with canned tomato, no onion/garlic (CUH, Glos bolognese 'no onion/garlic'); Stanford: marinara 'small amounts'; certified brands (Kaiser: FODY)
foods.highServing: virtually all jarred and restaurant pasta/cooking sauces (onion, garlic; CUH, UHS, Glos, Kaiser)

foods.name: salad dressing
foods.lowServing: oil and vinegar (Kaiser, Glos); low-FODMAP dressings without garlic/onion/HFCS (Stanford)
foods.highServing: most store-bought dressings (MNGI, Stanford, CUH, Glos): garlic, onion, HFCS, honey

foods.name: gravy
foods.lowServing: homemade stock/broth without onion/garlic (Stanford, Kaiser, CUH, Glos, MNGI)
foods.highServing: stock cubes, gravy granules, gravy browning, commercial broths and soups (IBS Diets, UHS, CUH, Glos, Kaiser)
foods.notes: FE 2017 lists 'soup concentrate (cubes)' low (some Monash-tested brands). Kaiser eating-out: avoid dishes made with stock/broth.
disagreements: FODMAP Everyday: soup concentrate cubes low
IBS Diets/UHS/CUH/Glos/Kaiser: stock cubes and gravy high

foods.name: soup
foods.highServing: canned/packet soups and ready meals (onion, garlic, wheat, cream) per CUH, Glos, UHS

foods.name: chutney
foods.lowServing: chutney 1 tbsp (IBS Diets); FE chutney low
foods.highServing: Stanford: chutneys, relish limit; IBS Diets: relish/vegetable pickle with onion high

foods.name: balsamic vinegar
foods.lowServing: 1-2 tbsp (IBS Diets 2 tbsp, Kaiser 1 tbsp, CUH <2 tbsp, Glos 1 tbsp, MNGI 1 tbsp)

foods.name: vinegar
foods.lowServing: unrestricted (apple cider vinegar 2 tbsp per IBS Diets)
foods.notes: FODMAP-free (malt vinegar FE2).

foods.name: sriracha
foods.highServing: larger amounts; many hot sauces contain garlic

foods.name: sweet and sour sauce
foods.notes: Check for HFCS in US versions.

foods.name: wasabi
foods.lowServing: wasabi powder low (CUH, FE, Kate grocery)
foods.highServing: IBS Diets lists 'wasabi' high (paste with additives)

foods.name: asafoetida
foods.notes: Onion-flavor substitute recommended by IBS Diets, CUH, Glos, FE.

foods.name: spice blend
foods.lowServing: pure single spices; curry powder without onion/garlic (FE, CUH); chili powder 100% chiles (Kaiser)
foods.highServing: most commercial blends contain onion and garlic powder (Kaiser, IBS Diets, Glos)

foods.name: olive oil
foods.notes: All pure oils are FODMAP-free (FE2, Kaiser, IBS Diets, CUH, Glos).

foods.name: sage
foods.notes: All fresh and dried herbs low (Kaiser, IBS Diets, CUH, Glos, MNGI).

foods.name: chili powder
foods.lowServing: unrestricted if 100% chiles (Kaiser; IBS Diets 'check for garlic')
foods.highServing: 'chili powder' blends with garlic/onion; MNGI: dried chipotle chili avoid
disagreements: IBS Diets: chipotle chili powder low

foods.name: salt
foods.notes: Garlic salt and onion salt are high.

foods.name: spirulina
foods.lowServing: spirulina unrestricted (FE2, CUH); maca 1 tsp; acai low (IBS Diets)

foods.name: dairy-free ice cream
foods.lowServing: sorbet 1/2 cup with allowed ingredients (Kaiser, MNGI); soy ice cream (Glos); rice milk ice cream (Stanford)
foods.highServing: versions sweetened with agave, apple juice, or polyols; mango/pear/apple sorbets

foods.name: sushi
foods.highServing: rolls with avocado in quantity, tempura (wheat), spicy mayo with garlic, eel sauce (HFCS)
foods.notes: Glos NHS lists sushi/sashimi as a suitable lunch and eating-out choice. Group inferred from typical add-ons.

foods.name: quesadilla
foods.lowServing: corn tortilla with cheddar, chicken, tomato (Stanford, MNGI, CUH meal ideas)
foods.highServing: flour tortilla; seasoning mixes with onion/garlic; refried beans

foods.name: risotto
foods.lowServing: Glos/CUH eating-out choice: request no onion/leek and check stock
foods.highServing: standard restaurant risotto (onion, stock cubes, sometimes mushrooms)

foods.name: french fries
foods.lowServing: plain potato fries/chips, hash browns (Glos, CUH, Kaiser)
foods.highServing: seasoned fries with onion/garlic powder; coated fries with wheat batter
